messages.author: 9ed4bd67fdbf8b5e
messages.subject: weird error
parts:
Hi all,

I'm running into an error parsing a text file in R, when the R-code is
evaluated via knit(). The code runs fine on its own. When run via knit
a CTRL-A is produced in the tex file instead of the required text, The
CTRL-A in turn kills pdflatex. Here's (fairly minimal) code and
sessionInfo:


\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}
<<test>>=
# make parameter file first
parfile <- 'partest.txt'
cat(file=parfile, "dir='/tmp/*'")
# now read and parse
lns <- readLines(parfile)
PAR <- vector('list', length=0)
for (l in strsplit(split='=', lns)) {
PAR[[l[1]]] <- l[2]
# fix for quoted strings
PAR[[l[1]]] <- gsub('^[\'\"](.*)[\'\"]$', '\\1', PAR[[l[1]]])
}
# print parameters for checking
cat(paste(names(PAR), PAR, sep='\t', collapse='\n'),'\n')
@
\end{document}



> sessionInfo()

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] weird error
parts:
Thanks for the report! It looks like a bug in the formatR package. I
will look into this issue.

At the moment, you can turn it off by <<test, tidy=FALSE>>=, and your
problem will be fixed.

Regards,
Yihui
